parsed.attack: CareZone is the same product and it is gone: a shared family ledger for an ageing parent's affairs, with one-tap photo and voice capture so logging was never the friction, used by hundreds of thousands of families. Walmart bought the technology for about $200 million in 2020, deactivated unmigrated consumer accounts on 31 January 2023, and shut Walmart Health entirely in April 2024. Its cause of death is the one this idea's own first kill criterion names - the ledger collapses onto the single sibling who already does everything, the second sibling never activates, and consumer willingness to pay never appeared, which is why every survivor in the category (Wellthy, ianacare) is sold to employers rather than to families. Flat-priced long context removes a retrieval pipeline; CareZone did not die of a retrieval pipeline, and Tandem's medication app [47] died of the same retention problem after research had validated the need.
parsed.strongest_defence: CareZone was a medication list first and a family record second, and the structured per-prescription data entry that made it a chore is genuinely replaced by thirty seconds of unstructured dictation from the car after a visit - a capture step that the non-primary sibling can actually complete.
parsed.verdict_reason: CareZone already had cheap capture and still died of the second sibling not participating and families not paying, and neither of those is touched by cheaper context.
